title: The Covariance Relaxation Produce Three Expansion Regimes of the Cosmic Evolution: A Conditional SL(6,C) Model of Populations, Metric Signatures and Gravity
content: We investigate how statistical covariance relaxation drives macroscopic cosmic evolution and metric-signature differentiation within a conditional SL(6,C) geometric-information framework. First, on the 35-dimensional positive statistical manifold, an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process calibrated to a physical clock yields exponential covariance-excess decay, and a root-space decomposition produces a three-to-one relaxation ratio under a specified weight condition. Second, coupling a positive vacuum-like response conservatively to a pressureless matter receiver in a flat Einstein-frame cosmology generates three ordered expansion regimes (early acceleration, intermediate dust-dominated deceleration, late dark-energy-driven acceleration) on an open parameter region. Third, using the same relaxing mode to parameterize embedded four-planes in a realified fibre induces metrics traversing three metric signatures, with an explicit anti-isometry exchanging the two Lorentzian sectors. Finally, quantitative interface and falsifiability tests separate geometric boundaries from cosmological transitions, including quantum reset channels, spectral-exclusion bounds and Grassmannian index obstructions that delimit statistical reduction, quantum completion and fermion multiplicity.
